newsitem.title: ALBANIA: ALBANIAN PARTIES STILL DIVIDED ON ELECTION LAW.
newsitem.headline: ALBANIAN PARTIES STILL DIVIDED ON ELECTION LAW.

text.p: Albanian political parties remained deeply divided over a new election law on Tuesday as Western officials tried last-minute talks to avoid the collapse of a deal aimed at paving the way to new elections.
The elections planned for the end of June are seen as vital to stop a repeat of the February and March riots that followed the collapse of pyramid investment schemes.
The parties were still rowing over a new election law, which was to have been approved yesterday by the nine main parties under a political contract brokered by European envoy Franz Vranitzky.
Under the deal, parliament must pass the law so President Sali Berisha can call a poll by May 15. The law says the president must call elections at least 45 days before voting.

But Socialist politicians said Berisha's ruling Democratic Party was trying to push a law through parliament on its own while the Socialists said it should be approved by the nine-party Government of National Reconciliation and then presented to parliament.

Differences remained unresolved over the proposed division of seats to be decided by proportional and majority voting, which has been at the centre of rows between the Democrats and the rest of the government.
